name: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Dermal Emission Suppressor
description:
The Dermal Emission Suppressor is a full-body compression underlayer embedded with a dense mesh of bioelectric regulation nodes developed from Zheng-Dao's research into autonomic system intervention. The underlayer interfaces non-invasively with the wearer's skin surface, monitoring galvanic response, localized surface temperature, and sweat gland activity across the body in real time. Using this data, the nodes apply targeted micro-current stimulation and localized thermoelectric cooling to suppress the involuntary physiological signals that thermal imaging, biometric stress sensors, and galvanic scan systems rely upon to detect and profile human presence.

The Suppressor's primary function is thermal: it maintains the wearer's skin surface temperature within 0.3 degrees of ambient environment temperature by dynamically redistributing body heat through a network of thermoelectric channels that terminate at a heat-sink collar worn at the back of the neck. This collar expels accumulated heat as a diffuse low-temperature plume rather than a concentrated body-shaped signature, dramatically reducing the wearer's profile on thermal imaging systems. A secondary function targets galvanic and stress-response suppression — the bioelectric nodes modulate skin conductivity to flatten the stress-response spikes that biometric scanners at corporate checkpoints use to flag persons of interest regardless of their visual identity.

Zheng-Dao markets a civilian variant of the underlying thermoelectric technology as a medical garment for patients with autonomic dysregulation disorders, which provides a plausible cover story for possession. The full Suppressor, however, exceeds medical specifications significantly and requires calibration to the wearer's specific bioelectric baseline — a process that takes approximately two hours and leaves a calibration record in Zheng-Dao's service network that cautious buyers pay considerable sums to have expunged.

specifications.thermal_suppression: Maintains skin surface within ±0.3°C of ambient; effective against thermal imaging up to Tier 4 military-grade systems
specifications.heat_sink_capacity: Maximum sustained heat dispersal: 180W; operational limit degrades in environments above 38°C ambient
specifications.galvanic_suppression: Reduces stress-response galvanic spike by 89% as measured by standard checkpoint biometric systems
specifications.calibration_time: 1.8 hours for full bioelectric baseline mapping
specifications.power_source: Passive thermoelectric harvest from body heat; supplemental micro-cell for node stimulation, 24-hour capacity
specifications.medical_cover_variant: Zheng-Dao Autonomic Comfort Layer — publicly registered, available Tier 1+

tactical_use: Essential for any operation requiring passage through environments with thermal surveillance — automated perimeter systems, drone overwatch, or facilities using thermal imaging as a primary detection layer. Equally valuable at biometric checkpoints where galvanic stress-response analysis is used to flag individuals regardless of forged visual credentials. The heat-sink collar requires the wearer to keep the back of the neck clear and unobstructed; operatives in close-quarters environments must be careful not to let the collar contact walls or other surfaces, which can transfer a detectable heat signature. Performance degrades significantly in high-ambient-temperature environments, making the Suppressor poorly suited to outdoor operations in hot climates.
cultural_context: The Suppressor occupies an uncomfortable legal space — technically licensed rather than prohibited, on the basis that Zheng-Dao's lobbying successfully framed it as a medical adjacent device. This means possession alone is not grounds for detention, but use in the vicinity of a security incident dramatically changes the legal calculus. Corporate security personnel are trained to recognize the heat-sink collar as a specific indicator, leading to an aftermarket in collar cosmetic covers that make it resemble standard medical or environmental neck bracing. Within the operative community, the Suppressor has a reputation as the mark of someone who plans ahead — acquiring and calibrating one requires patience and resources that impulsive operators rarely possess.
known_users: High-value couriers moving through thermal surveillance corridors
Patients with genuine autonomic disorders (civilian variant)
Dae-Sung Lim — former Zheng-Dao calibration technician turned independent contractor
Extraction teams operating in facilities with automated thermal perimeter systems
story_hooks: A calibration record that was supposed to be expunged wasn't — someone at Zheng-Dao kept a copy, and now the operative's bioelectric baseline is being used to identify them at scenes they were never supposed to be connected to.

A job requires passing through a thermal-monitored zone in a 42°C industrial environment — the Suppressor will fail halfway through, and the team needs an alternative plan for the second half of the route.

A body is found in a thermal-blind zone with a Suppressor still active on the corpse — whoever killed them knew the body wouldn't register on the facility's thermal sweep for hours, buying time to escape.

Zheng-Dao quietly recalls a batch of Suppressors citing a 'calibration firmware issue' — operatives who ignore the recall notice start experiencing involuntary muscle contractions during high-stress situations at unpredictable intervals.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting full-body compression underlayer resembling high-tech athletic wear. The garment clings to the torso, limbs, and torso with surgical precision. A distinctive hinged heat-sink collar protrudes from the back of the neck—a polished metallic component roughly the size of a closed fist, with visible micro-vents arranged in concentric circles. The overall silhouette reads as medical-grade performance wear, deliberately ambiguous between therapeutic and tactical.
physical_description.dimensions: Full-body garment; collar component approximately 8cm wide × 6cm tall × 4cm deep; worn as a second skin under standard clothing
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight and pocketable when compressed; 1.4kg total, distributed across the body—barely noticeable when worn. Collar adds minimal neck strain.
physical_description.primary_material: Bioelectric-responsive smart textile base (synthetic polymer blend with embedded conductive mesh); heat-sink collar is brushed titanium-aluminum composite
physical_description.finish: Matte compression fabric with a subtle iridescent sheen visible only under direct light, suggesting embedded circuitry. Collar features micro-etched cooling vents with satin finish; internal surfaces show faint traces of thermal paste around node junctions
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray compression layer with muted silver node points visible as raised dimples across chest, shoulders, and spine. Heat-sink collar in brushed gunmetal gray with faint blue LED indicators along the vent edges (inactive until powered)
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimalist design: small recessed charging port (USB-C) at the base of collar; single capacitive touch zone on the left shoulder for calibration mode activation; discrete status indicator (three-LED array) hidden beneath collar rim; no visible screens or aggressive controls
distinctive_features: Hinged heat-sink collar with concentric cooling vents that articulate slightly during operation
Raised bioelectric node points across the garment surface—subtle texture like acupuncture meridian mapping
Faint copper-colored conductive pathways visible at seams and junction points under close inspection
Thermal gradation visible on collar surface during use—cooler at vents, warmer at base
Internal neck webbing with calibration contact points
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC logo embroidered in metallic thread at the shoulder seam (small, 2cm); regulatory stamp stating 'MEDICAL AUTONOMIC SUPPORT LAYER' and compliance certifications at the collar base; serial number etched subtly into underside of collar
physical_description.condition_typical: When worn under clothing, only the collar is visible—appearing as an unusual but plausible medical device. In stealth use, the garment is worn with minimal upper body coverage to maximize heat dissipation through the collar. After extended use (2+ hours), micro-condensation may bead on collar vents. Unit shows slight wear at contact points after sustained calibration cycles.
